text:
maya: Heads-up — I'm drafting a modular rollback playbook for catalog migrations. Want to capture: canary lanes, soft vs hard rollbacks, customer opt-ins, communication windows, and benchmark gating.
sam: Nice. Do you mean per-model lanes or per-tenant?
maya: per-model by default, but with per-tenant overrides (customers with contracts can pin). Keep default behavior safe for GA.
tj: For benchmarks we should define both perf and quality gates. e.g., latency p95, token cost delta, and a quality regression metric (BLEU/ROUGE or eval-set pass-rate).
elaine: Also need TTL for pins. Customers often ask for a 30/90 day soft pin, then renegotiate. Hard pins should be rare and require legal signoff.
maya: Agreed. Proposal: soft-pin TTL = 30d auto-renew opt-in, hard-pin = manual SOW.
sam: Regarding canaries: propose 3 phased lanes -> shadow, 5% canary, 25% ramp. Each phase has an automated monitor and automatic rollback if thresholds breach.
tj: Putting some concrete thresholds in the thread to discuss:
```
canary_policy:
  shadow: true
  canary_step_1: 5%
  canary_step_2: 25%
  monitors: [p95_latency, cost_per_token, eval_pass_rate]
  rollback_triggers:
    - eval_pass_rate_drop_pct: 3
    - p95_latency_increase_pct: 15
    - cost_increase_pct: 25
```
elaine: Sounds reasonable. For eval_pass_rate we need stable eval sets by tenant cohort (search, chat, summarization). Who owns those sets?
maya: product owns canonical eval sets, customer-specific probes live with SEs and Solutions. We need a map in the playbook linking tenant -> probe set.
sam: Communication plan: 72h pre-notice for non-critical migrations, immediate notice + status channel for emergency rollbacks. Also provide a one-click opt-out toggle in Console.
tj: Ops/infra notes: KV cache mismatch is a common issue after model swap, we should include a cache-flush hint and a lightweight compatibility check to run in shadow mode.
elaine: Also add a fallback policy: if a model is deprecated, auto-route to nearest compatible variant (same family, lower-cost quantized) unless tenant is pinned. That preserves availability.
maya: Good. Also need billing safety: stop billing for new tokens during rollback until state reconciled, track delta in chargeback report.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout initiated for model m-ceres-v2 -> m-ceres-v3 at 2023-09-12T15:04Z (job 5821). Monitoring hooks enabled.
sam: For the playbook doc we need clear runbook sections: preflight checklist, canary config, monitoring thresholds, rollback steps, customer comm templates, postmortem template.
tj: Add a short snippet for immediate rollback command so oncall can run it quickly:
```sh
# rollback to previous model
redwoodctl rollout cancel --model m-ceres-v3 --to m-ceres-v2 --reason "canary breach"
```
elaine: Also include a migration credit policy: if customer sees >3% quality regression they get a one-time credit and priority remediation.
maya: Assign owners: Sam -> canary automation and console toggle. Ela ine -> customer comm templates and pin TTL policy. TJ -> monitor definitions and rollback scripts. I'll assemble the initial playbook draft by EOD Friday.
sam: I can pair with infra on the console toggle tomorrow.
tj: Will sketch monitor dashboards and alert thresholds today.
elaine: I'll draft email + support KB + FAQ.
maya: Great — let's sync Fri 10am to review draft. If anyone spots gaps in the meantime drop comments here. :thumbsup:
